question: Why is the means here also not a means?
premises: This means is also a non-means because it blocks effortful activity.
It is devoid of exhalation and inhalation practices.
It is devoid of regulation of body and breath.
inference: The so-called means transcends ordinary technique by abandoning effortful bodily and breath controls.
uncertainties: The exact analysis of tanuvātanauḥ is compressed in the transmitted form.
plain_english: Even the means is not a means, because it stops effortful activity; it is free from exhalation and inhalation and from the regulation of body and breath.
